title: SHIFT - A One-Button Game About Gears
short: Shift is the only control. Hold it for high gear: fast, committed, clears wide gaps. Let go for low gear: slow, gripping, fits through the gates. Gaps need speed. Gates punish it.
description:
The theme is SHIFT. So Shift is the only button.

A Game Off 2026 entry on the theme SHIFT.

Two gears, and they disagree

  • HOLD SHIFT - high gear. Fast, carries momentum, clears wide gaps. It also will not stop in time.
  • LET GO - low gear. Slow, grips the ground, fits through narrow gates. It also will never make the jump.

You never steer. The course arrives. Gaps need speed. Gates punish it. Every decision in a run is hold or let go, several hundred times, and the two demands are always in the way of each other. That is the whole game.

Controls

  • SHIFT (or space, or J) - hold for high gear, release for low
  • ENTER - start, and retry
  • ESC - pause   R - restart

That is the entire interface. There is no steering, no jump, no attack.

Why it is one button

Because the theme offered three readings and this is the strictest one. If the only thing you can do is shift, then the game is entirely about when - which is what shifting gears actually is. A gearbox does not give you new abilities; it changes what your existing speed is good for.

Tested, and what the tests assert

29 assertions run headless. The interesting ones are design assertions rather than plumbing:

  • low cruise really is slower than high cruise, so the button does something
  • high gear takes several frames to build, so committing costs time
  • braking from high gear does not stop instantly, so commitment costs something else too
  • a gap cannot be cleared at low cruise and can be at high - and a gate is the exact inverse
  • the design is fair: every obstacle is passable in some gear, none is passable in all of them
  • the course is valid: obstacles inside bounds and spaced so a player can recover
  • the same seed produces the same course, so a bug is reproducible

The scene boots headless with no script errors. A web build is attached, plus a Windows build.

Where the assets came from

Built on the Gen XIA toolkit:

  • Dread - Horror HUD & UI Kit - the cockpit panels and palette
  • Dread - Horror & Survival SFX - the sounds
  • Gen XIA Character Library - sprite reference

Source is public with credits in the README, as the jam rules require.

AI disclosure

AI-assisted. Design, code and every final file are decided by hand; generative tooling was part of the pipeline.
